title: Mouth opening after fibula free flap reconstruction: Impact of radiation and implications for prosthodontic rehabilitation
html: Mandibular mobility is critical for prosthodontic rehabilitation following maxillofacial reconstruction, especially in a procedure like Jaw-in-a-Day (JIAD) that needs accurate pre-operative planning. The fibula free flap (FFF) reconstruction enables the restoration of appearance and function after benign or neoplastic tumor resection, but some complications, such as trismus, present in a delayed manner or worsen after radiotherapy (RT). The specific magnitude of reduction in maximum incisal opening (MIO) following these procedures is poorly quantified, potentially compromising the feasibility of definitive prosthetic delivery, maintenance, and long-term survivability.
